title: Introduce invoke-signal affinity and streamed schema annotations for OpenAI-compatible function calls
author: Aisha Martinez
description: Motivation: We observed intermittent misattribution of tool/function selections when streaming fragments arrive out-of-order across adaptive multiplexing paths. This causes downstream tooling to receive ambiguous "tool_choice" signals and occasionally a malformed JSON payload when fragments are stitched. This PR introduces a lightweight per-fragment 'invoke signal' header and a deterministic affinity rule that binds fragments from the same logical function call to a single coalescer. The change reduces mis-selection and stabilizes structured outputs for OpenAI-compatible function/tool calling. Summary of changes: 1) Protocol: add an optional 'x-invoke-signal' field in stream frames that carries a stable 8-char affinity token plus sequence index and optional schema-hash. 2) Router/runtime: wire affinity token into the fragment coalescer; fragments with the same token are preferentially routed to the same aggregator instance while still allowing fallback routing under load. 3) Schema annotations: during coalescing we emit a single canonical 'function_call' JSON envelope with an embedded 'schema_annotations' array that maps original tool schema fields to observed fragments. 4) Backcompat: tokens are optional; frames without the header continue to be handled by existing heuristics. 5) Telemetry: add metrics for affinity hit/miss, fragment-latency, and schema-repair counts. Testing and validation: - Unit tests for tokenizer and affinity assignment (router unit tests). - Integration test harness that replays recorded multiplexed streams (new test: tests/stream/coalesce_affinity_replay.test). - End-to-end: ran canary on perf-canary with synthetic traffic; saw 87% reduction in misattributed tool_choice events and 22% p95 improvement in structured output assembly latency. Checklist: - [x] Protocol change documented in API compatibility notes - [x] Runtime changes behind feature flag 'invoke-affinity-v1' - [x] Add telemetry & dashboards - [x] Backcompat regression run - [x] Docs: added section to /docs/openai-compat/streamed-invoke.md Rollout plan: enable feature flag for internal tenants and beta customers for one week; monitor affinity-miss and schema-repair metrics; if <1% affinity-miss and no schema-repair errors increase rollout to GA. Risks and mitigations: risk of traffic skew causing hot-spotting of coalescer instances; mitigation: token-space salted with instance id and fallbacks to capacity-aware routing. Related work: ENG-17420 (fragment coalescer refactor), previous RFCs around tool_choice semantics. Notes: this intentionally keeps 'tool_choice' semantics unchanged in API surface; it only provides stronger signal on the wire for the coalescer and telemetry for debugging.

review_conversation: Liam Chen: Please ensure we have deterministic hashing and note collision probability in the protocol doc. Author: used truncated blake2b with 64 bits and added collision telemetry.
Sofia Patel: Is there any PSAT impact? Author: synthetic perf tests show negligible CPU overhead; added p95 latency results to the PR description.
Marco Ruiz: Can we make the header optional to avoid breaking older proxies? Author: header is optional; documented fallback behavior and added feature flag.
release_notes: Adds optional per-frame 'x-invoke-signal' affinity token to stabilize streamed function/tool call assembly; runtime feature-flagged as 'invoke-affinity-v1'. Improves tool selection accuracy and structured output assembly latency. Backwards compatible with older clients.
